info.name: Bigfoot Express Freight API
info.description:
# Bigfoot Express Freight - API Collection

This collection wraps the **Parcel Perfect Ecommerce Service (JSON API, v27)** that powers Bigfoot Express Freight's customer-facing shipping API. It lets customers get quotes, look up places/postcodes, submit collections and waybills, and retrieve tracking/waybill details, directly from Postman.

## Getting started
1. Import both this collection and the companion **Bigfoot Express Freight - My Account** environment, then select that environment in Postman's top-right environment picker. Fill in your `email`, `password` and `accnum` in the environment (ask Bigfoot Express Freight for your account credentials if you don't have them). Also update the collection's `baseUrl` variable to your production service URL - it defaults to Parcel Perfect's public demo endpoint, which only accepts demo credentials.
2. Run **1. Authentication > 1 - Get Salt**, then **2 - Get Secure Token**. The token is saved automatically and reused by every other request in this collection for the next ~24 hours.
3. Use **2. Places Lookup** to resolve your origin/destination postcodes or town names into the `place`/`town` values the API expects.
4. Either:
   - **Quote first**: `3. Quotes > Request Quote` -> `Update Service` -> `Convert Quote To Waybill` / `Convert Quote To Collection`, or
   - **Submit directly**: `4. Collections > Submit Collection` / `Submit Compound Collection`.
5. Use `5. Waybills > Get Single Waybill` to check on a shipment afterwards.

## How the API works
Every call is an HTTP `GET` to `baseUrl` with three (or four) query parameters:
- `class` - the API class, e.g. `Auth`, `Quote`, `Collection`
- `method` - the method to call on that class, e.g. `getSalt`, `requestQuote`
- `params` - a JSON-encoded object of parameters for that method
- `token_id` - your auth token, required on every call except `getSalt` and `getSecureToken`

Every response has the same envelope:
```json
{ "errorcode": 0, "errormessage": "", "results": [ { ... } ] }
```
`errorcode` is `0` on success; any other value means `errormessage` describes what went wrong.

## Source material
The requests in this collection were built from the reference PHP/SOAP examples and the full field-level API specification (`Parcel Perfect Ecommerce Service - v27.pdf` / `.xlsx`) under `refs/API/Parcel Perfect/` in this repository - refer to those for the complete list of optional fields (insurance, customs, surcharge flags, multi-page references, etc.) not shown in the example payloads here.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description:
The Bigfoot Express Freight API (powered by Parcel Perfect's Ecommerce Service) uses a salt + MD5 + token authentication flow:

1. **Get Salt** - fetch a one-time salt for your account
2. **Get Secure Token** - hash your password with the salt and exchange it for a token
3. Use the returned token (`{{token}}`) as the `token_id` query parameter on every subsequent call

Run requests 1 and 2 in order at the start of every session (or whenever your token expires - tokens are valid for roughly 24 hours). Set your `email` and `password` collection variables first.

request.description:
Step 1 of authentication. Returns a random salt used to build the MD5 password hash required by **Get Secure Token**.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| email | M | The username (normally an email address) used for authentication |

On success, the returned `salt` is saved to the collection variable `salt` automatically so you don't need to copy it manually.

Step 2 of authentication. Exchanges your password (MD5-hashed with the salt from **Get Salt**) for a secure token. The token is required on almost every other call in this collection (sent as the `token_id` query parameter).

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| email | M | The username used for authentication |
| password | M | MD5 hash of `password + salt` |

A pre-request script computes the MD5 hash automatically from the `password` and `salt` collection variables, so just run **Get Salt** first, then run this request. The returned token is saved to the collection variable `token` automatically.

exec: console.warn('No salt found - run "1 - Get Salt" first.');
// API docs and sample code disagree on the field name, handle both

request.description: Checks whether the token currently stored in the `token` collection variable is still valid (tokens expire after 24 hours). Not covered in the formal v27 spec document but used in Parcel Perfect's own sample code - if your account returns an error, request a fresh token instead using **Get Salt** and **Get Secure Token**.

Manually expires (logs out) the token currently stored in the `token` collection variable. Useful for cleanly ending a session.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| token_id | The token to expire |

item.name: 2. Places Lookup
item.description: Before submitting a quote, collection or waybill you need the internal `place` code and `town` name for both the origin and destination. Use these two requests to resolve a postcode or a town name into that pair of values.

request.description:
Looks up valid place/town codes for a given postcode. The returned `place` (internal town code) and `town` name are required when building quotes, collections and waybills (`origplace`/`origtown` or `destplace`/`desttown`).

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| postcode | M | Postcode to search for |

Looks up valid place/town codes by name or partial name. Use this when you know the town/suburb name but not its postcode.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| name | M | Name or partial name to search for |

item.name: 3. Quotes
item.description: Standard quoting workflow: **Request Quote** to get rates for a shipment, **Update Service** to lock in the service you want, then convert the quote into either a **Waybill** (you deliver/drop off) or a **Collection** (Bigfoot collects from you).

request.description:
Requests a freight quote for a shipment. Requires the `origplace`/`origtown` and `destplace`/`desttown` from **Places Lookup**, plus at least one contents line with `actmass` > 0 (a rate will not calculate otherwise).

**Mandatory fields**: `details`, `contents` (each line needs `pieces`, `description`, `actmass`, `item`), `ttype` (defaults to `I` for insert).

The response contains an array of `rates`, one per available service - pick one and pass its `service` code to **Update Service**. The `quoteno` is saved automatically to the `quoteno` collection variable.

Sets which transport service to use on a previously requested quote, and returns the final calculated rate for that service.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| quoteno | M | Quote number returned by Request Quote |
| service | M | 3-character service code, e.g. one from the `rates` array |
| reference | | Customer reference |

Converts a priced quote (after **Update Service**) into a real waybill.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| quoteno | M | Quote number previously generated by Request Quote |
| specins | | Special instructions |
| printWaybill | | 1 = return a base64-encoded waybill PDF |
| printLabels | | 1 = return a base64-encoded labels PDF |

Set `printWaybill`/`printLabels` to `1` and use the **Visualize** tab in Postman to preview the returned PDF inline.

Converts a priced quote (after **Update Service**) into a collection request, so Bigfoot Express Freight will collect the shipment from you.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| quoteno | M | Quote number previously generated by Request Quote |
| starttime | | Collection window start time, `hh:mm:ss` |
| endtime | | Collection window end time, `hh:mm:ss` |
| quoteCollectionDate | | Collection date, `dd.mm.yyyy` |
| notes | | Notes for the collection |
| specins | | Special instructions |
| printWaybill | | 1 = return a base64-encoded waybill PDF |
| printLabels | | 1 = return a base64-encoded labels PDF |

item.name: 4. Collections
item.description: Submit collection requests directly (skipping the quote step). Use **Submit Collection** for a single waybill, or **Submit Compound Collection** to collect several waybills bound for different destinations in one run.

request.description:
Directly submits a waybill and collection request in a single call, without going through the quote workflow first. Use this once you know exactly which service and account number you're shipping with.

**Mandatory fields (details)**: `service`, `collectiondate`, `origpers`, `origperadd1`, `origtown`, `origperpcode`, `origpercontact`, `origperphone`, `destpers`, `destperadd1`, `desttown`, `destperpcode`, `destpercontact`, `destperphone`.

**Mandatory fields (each contents line)**: `pieces`, `description`, `actmass`, `item`. At least one contents line with `actmass` > 0 is required.

request.description:
Submits a single collection covering **multiple waybills** (multiple destinations picked up from one origin in one collection run). Each entry in `waybills` has its own `details` (destination) and `contents`, and may optionally include `wayrefs` (extra references) and `tracks` (tracking numbers).

This is the JSON equivalent of the `submitCompoundCollection` SOAP/JSON method - see the reference PHP examples under `refs/API/Parcel Perfect/` for a fully worked example including tracking numbers and surcharge flags.

item.name: 5. Waybills
item.description: Look up an existing waybill by number.

request.description:
Retrieves the full details, contents, tracking numbers and references for a single waybill.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| waybillno | M | Waybill number |

_Note: the class for this method is inferred as `Waybill` from the naming convention used by other methods (e.g. `Auth`, `Quote`, `Collection`) - it is not shown in a worked example. If you get a class-not-found style error, check with Bigfoot/Parcel Perfect support for the correct class name._

item.name: 6. Default Content Items
item.description: Look up pre-configured default parcel/contents templates for your account.

request.description:
Retrieves your account's pre-configured default contents items (if your account has any set up by Bigfoot Express Freight) - useful for reusing common parcel dimensions/weights instead of typing them out on every request.

**Params (JSON)**
| Field | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|
| name | M | Default content item name to search for |

_Note: the class for this method is inferred as `Quote` - if you get a class-not-found style error, check with Bigfoot/Parcel Perfect support for the correct class name._
